newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks Iraqi Kurd support against rebels.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks Iraqi Kurd support against rebels.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller met Iraqi Kurdish leader Jalal Talabani on Thursday to seek his cooperation in Ankara's fight against Kurdish rebels who use northern Iraq as a base to attack Turkey.

"Talabani and Barzani groups see it is a necessity to act against the PKK (Kurdistan Workers Party) to bring peace to the region (northern Iraq)," Ciller told reporters after the meeting, without giving details.
The PKK rebels use bases in northern Iraq, outside Baghdad's control since 1991, as part of its 12-year-old guerrilla war for self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
More than 21,000 people have died in the conflict. Large numbers of Turkish troops have crossed into Iraq on several occasions in pursuit of the guerrillas.
Talabani expressed support for Ciller's proposal.

"We will keep trying to secure Turkey's border (with Iraq). Our people is not accepting the existence of any military groups in Iraq Kurdistan...against Turkey," said Talabani, whose Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) controls part of northern Iraq.
The meeting between Ciller and Talabani followed two days of peace talks in Ankara between the PUK and the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) of Massoud Barzani.

Talabani arrived in Turkey after the talks, which were brokered by officials from the United States, Turkey and Britain. The talks brought agreement to improve conditions for civilians harmed by the fighting between the two groups.

The KDP and PUK agreed to a U.S.-mediated ceasefire last October after clashes that escalated when the KDP joined with Iraqi troops to take control of the key Kurdish city of Arbil from Talabani's fighters at the end of August.
The clashes gave Baghdad a foothold in Western-protected northern Iraq for the first time since the end of the 1991 Gulf War, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
